title: Germany raises Deutschlandticket price to €66.80 a month from 2027 under new cost-based formula
summary: A new cost-based formula has pushed up the price of Germany's nationwide public transport pass for 2027.

image.caption: The Deutschlandticket is set to become more expensive again from January 2027 (FILE: 17/12/2025)Image: Thorsten Wagner/W2Art/picture alliance

blocks.text: Germany's nationwide Deutschlandticket will cost €66.80 ($78) per month from January 1, 2027, up from the current €63, transport authorities said on Wednesday.
It is the first price increase to be determined using a new cost-based formula rather than through political negotiations between Germany's federal and state governments.
Why is the Deutschlandticket getting more expensive?

The €3.80 increase reflects rising personnel, energy and other operating costs, according to Bavaria's Transport Ministry, which currently chairs the conference of Germany's state transport ministers.
The new formula also takes into account that federal and state subsidies remain fixed at a combined €3 billion ($3.5 billion) a year.
The discounted job ticket will rise to €63.46, while the student semester ticket will cost €40.08.
Rising fuel prices put pressure on German drivers
Federal Transport Minister Steffen Bilger, of the conservative Christian Democratic Union, said the ticket remained "a very attractive offer" despite the increase.
Around 14.5 million people currently use the Deutschlandticket, which covers local and regional public transport across Germany.
It was launched at €49 a month in 2023 and currently costs €63. The new price means the ticket will have become around 36% more expensive since its launch.
North Rhine-Westphalia Transport Minister Oliver Krischer, of the environmentalist Greens, criticized the increase, saying the federal government had promised price stability.
